purpose: REQUIRED-CONFIGURATION SPECIFICATION for the platform-enforced trusted runner isolation of the real-VFP9 acceptance lane. This file is NOT evidence of configuration and NOT evidence of execution: it states the security boundary that MUST hold before any trusted self-hosted VFP9 execution may ever be scheduled. It deliberately separates the immutable REQ-P7-006 repository CI/isolation acceptance from the CONDITIONAL real-VFP9 execution evidence that only requirements explicitly demanding it (especially REQ-P6-003) may use.

acceptance_separation.note: Two evidence classes that must never be conflated: the repository CI/isolation acceptance of REQ-P7-006 and the conditional real-VFP9 execution evidence of REQ-P6-003.

req_p7_006_repository_ci_isolation_accep.immutable_acceptance_evidence: version-controlled workflows and green mandatory jobs
criteria: every mandatory CI category (format, lint, strict typecheck, compile, unit, integration, property/privacy, relationship, recovery, transfer-bundle, malformed-input, package, security) is version-controlled in this repository
every declared Python version is covered on Windows hosted runners
a no-VFP cross-platform hosted smoke path exists
the trusted self-hosted VFP9 check path is isolated from untrusted pull-request code
all mandatory hosted jobs are green on the exact reviewed HEAD
req_p7_006_repository_ci_isolation_accep.note: The absence of a currently provisioned trusted self-hosted VFP runner does NOT make REQ-P7-006 PARTIAL when this isolation contract is objectively present and no unsafe execution occurs. External runner provisioning is NOT a mandatory REQ-P7-006 closure stage, and the absence of live VFP execution does not invalidate this repository-side acceptance.

conditional_real_vfp_execution_evidence.note: Real Visual FoxPro 9 execution on a trusted Windows runner is CONDITIONAL acceptance evidence for requirements that explicitly demand it (especially REQ-P6-003). It is NOT a REQ-P7-006 closure gate, and provisioning external runner infrastructure is NOT required to close REQ-P7-006.

canonical_selected_workflow.placeholder_note: FINAL_OWNER is deliberately unset because the repository ownership/topology decision has not been made. Before any live verification, the platform owner must replace the placeholder with the actual owner in the live runner-group configuration; the repository never guesses it.
canonical_selected_workflow.github_note: GitHub runner-group workflow restrictions require a fully qualified workflow identity (owner/repository/path@ref); the template above corresponds to that format.

layer_1_platform_authorization.group_membership: self-hosted Windows runner dedicated to Visual FoxPro 9 acceptance

repository_access.owner_placeholder_note: FINAL_OWNER is deliberately unset until the repository ownership/topology decision is made; it must not be guessed.
repository_access.default_scope_note: By default private repositories only can access a runner group; public access must be granted explicitly and deliberately.

workflow_access.equivalent_platform_isolation: acceptable only if it provably prevents every other workflow file - including future PR-modified files - from scheduling jobs on the trusted runner

layer_1_platform_authorization.verification_procedure: After provisioning, verify through GitHub configuration APIs/settings (runner group exists; repository allowlist == the single DBF_Anonymizer repository; workflow allowlist exactly the canonical selected workflow pinned to refs/heads/main) and only then dispatch the trusted workflow on refs/heads/main to produce conditional REQ-P6-003 execution evidence.

layer_2_workflow_defense_in_depth.ref_guard: refs/heads/main only, verified before any checkout
layer_2_workflow_defense_in_depth.checkout: no explicit ref and no caller-provided SHA/branch; never github.event.pull_request.head.sha
layer_2_workflow_defense_in_depth.revision_identity: git rev-parse HEAD must equal origin/main and be recorded with the sanitized evidence
layer_2_workflow_defense_in_depth.acceptance_tool: tools/run_real_vfp9_acceptance.py (the established REQ-P6-003 boundary; no second acceptance protocol)

runner_targeting.syntax: runs-on mapping with group and labels
runner_targeting.fail_closed: while either variable is unset the job cannot be scheduled and the lane produces no evidence

layer_2_workflow_defense_in_depth.environment_approvals: NOT a substitute for the runner-group boundary (an attacker-controlled workflow could omit the environment)

branch_protection_note: This specification does not assert GitHub branch-protection enforcement. Effective required-status-check enforcement is an external platform setting that must be verified from live platform configuration before relying on it; the trusted lane's own ref guard (LAYER 2) is the repository-side isolation mechanism.

stable_topology_constraints.note: Normative facts that hold under the CURRENT topology and must be re-evaluated when ownership/topology changes.

external_observation.note: Point-in-time observation with provenance; NOT_LIVE_EVIDENCE — do not treat as continuously valid GitHub state. Volatile counts belong here, never among normative facts.

invariants: no repository-level self-hosted runner workaround: the trusted lane may only target a platform-authorized runner group
the trusted workflow is workflow_dispatch-only and refuses every ref except refs/heads/main before any checkout
no caller-provided SHA or pull-request ref is ever checked out; the checked-out revision is verified against origin/main and the canonical architecture hash
runner targeting is fail-closed: group and labels are read only from the authoritative repository variables; no literal group or label is committed to the repository
the real-VFP9 lane delegates all acceptance semantics to tools/run_real_vfp9_acceptance.py and never executes untrusted pull-request code

GitHub accepts workflow_dispatch events only for workflow files on the default branch, so the trusted workflow becomes dispatchable once it is merged to the default branch; that fact alone changes no acceptance status of any requirement
